Games are more than the things we play. They are people, inventions and places that stay with us. Pixel Museum brings their stories into one collection for you to explore.
strings.The story of play sits beside a wider hi: The story of play sits beside a wider history of technology, culture and world events. Switching timelines takes you to the closest date, revealing what happened around the same time.
strings.Exhibits unfold through photographs, arc: Exhibits unfold through photographs, archive films, music and original interactive experiences. Explore their cards, listen to a score or put an idea into motion. Longer passages can be read in place.

strings.Pong makes anticipation visible through: Pong makes anticipation visible through a ball, a paddle and the space between them. Move this original paddle study to discover how the point of contact changes the next return.
strings.Breakout turns each removed brick into a: Breakout turns each removed brick into a change in the ball's possible route. Steer this original paddle exercise and watch how a small opening can change the rhythm of an entire rally.
strings.Space Invaders organises pressure throug: Space Invaders organises pressure through an approaching formation and the timing of a shot. Move and fire in this original pattern study. A passing mothership offers a bonus above the formation: aiming for it means briefly leaving the nearer threat unattended.
strings.Pac-Man gives a junction meaning by plac: Pac-Man gives a junction meaning by placing routes, pursuit and a goal in the same small space. Queue turns while movement continues in this original looping board. Clear the dots, read three different pursuers and decide when a power light or temporary fruit is worth a detour.
strings.Tetris makes the shape of an empty space: Tetris makes the shape of an empty space as important as the shape falling towards it. Move and rotate pieces in this original packing study, using the landing guide to compare a quick fit with a decision that leaves room for the next piece.
strings.Spacewar! makes inertia and a central gr: Spacewar! makes inertia and a central gravitational pull part of steering a spacecraft. Turn, thrust and brake in this original navigation study to compare the direction you face with the route your movement actually follows.
strings.Elite uses wireframe edges to make a thr: Elite uses wireframe edges to make a three-dimensional world readable without painted surfaces. Follow 120 approaching openings in this original depth study: their growing edges pass around your flight line, while a quiet pointer identifies the next opening. Small corrections made early are easier than a late turn. Hold the controller still briefly, then tilt to steer; the stick remains available. The route waits while the controller finds its neutral pose.
strings.Sonic the Hedgehog makes acceleration an: Sonic the Hedgehog makes acceleration and momentum part of reading a route. Build speed on an original rolling landscape, carry momentum through a full loop and a low curved tunnel, jump its gaps or take the higher ledges. Braking deliberately sheds speed. At rest, combine braking with repeated jumps to charge a rolling start; release the brake to spend that stored motion. The checkpoint banks your rings, so a risky route has something to lose. A clear, level finishing straight gives you room to reach the spinning sign after the final obstacles.
strings.Celeste turns a jump and one short air d: Celeste turns a jump and one short air dash into a sequence of commitments. Cross five original platforming rooms: clear a gap, touch a floating diamond to restore the dash in midair, then climb between safe ledges. Landing restores the dash too. A dotted arrow shows the direction you are aiming; the small diamond shows when another dash is available. Each lit doorway saves the next room, so a fall only repeats the current challenge.
strings.Dance Dance Revolution connects a repeat: Dance Dance Revolution connects a repeated beat to a precise window for action. Tap through this original rhythm study to hear and see the difference between matching a pulse and reacting after it.
strings.Lumines makes a musical scanline decide: Lumines makes a musical scanline decide when a matching visual pattern clears. Arrange two-by-two colour groups in this original grid study and listen to how a timed sweep joins a spatial choice to a musical event.
strings.Wolfenstein 3D constructs a first-person: Wolfenstein 3D constructs a first-person view by measuring distances across a map. Find three survey marks in an original corridor map and compare the plan with the wall heights that make it appear deep. The same space is read from above and at eye level.
strings.Katamari Damacy makes a growing body cha: Katamari Damacy makes a growing body change the meaning of the same surroundings. Roll and gather smaller objects in this original scale study to see an object that first resists collection become something you can gather.
strings.Portal makes momentum part of a spatial: Portal makes momentum part of a spatial puzzle. Connect marked surfaces in five original chambers: cross a wall, turn a fall into distance, carry a cube onto an upper pressure plate, send a cube through a ceiling portal to open a remote door, then build speed in a floor-to-ceiling loop and redirect it toward a high exit. Speed survives each crossing while its direction follows the portal. A dotted arc previews the current route. Choose surfaces with the right stick or touchpad; carry and release the cube nearby. Pressure plates stay active only while supporting the cube.
strings.Gunpei Yokoi's approach to portable play: Gunpei Yokoi's approach to portable play makes constraints part of the design. Balance shades, motion, light and sound in an original prototype, then test three different briefs. The costs are illustrative design units, not measurements of historical hardware. The touchpad lets a design change beneath your finger.
strings.Koji Kondo treats music as part of how a: Koji Kondo treats music as part of how a game communicates action. Guide an original figure along a route and listen as rest, walking and running change the density of an original D-minor phrase. Its clock keeps moving instead of restarting at each change. Collect twelve lights and reach the flag.
strings.Shigeru Miyamoto's platform games invite: Shigeru Miyamoto's platform games invite close attention to how a character moves. Tune gravity, lift and air control in this original jump laboratory, reach three flags and compare the pale trace of a previous landing with your next attempt. A short tap and a held jump produce different arcs.
strings.SimCity invites a player to think in con: SimCity invites a player to think in connected systems. In this original workshop, draw roads between homes, workplaces and a clinic, keep green space nearby, and follow the travelling dots. Change a route to see how journey length and congestion affect three construction briefs. These budgets and rules are illustrative, rather than a simulation of a real city.
strings.Game Boy artwork builds a legible image: Game Boy artwork builds a legible image from a small grid and four shades. Edit this original eight-by-eight drawing to see how changing one square can suggest an edge, a curve or the space between them.
strings.Interface foundation — ps5-homebrew-ui b: Interface foundation — ps5-homebrew-ui by BlackBearReloaded. Its OpenGL renderer, type system, springs, controller components and image viewer form the museum interface.

strings.General credits full text:
Thanks to my father for passing on his passion for technology. Thanks to my mother for giving me the sensitivity to appreciate art and look at the world with wonder. Thanks to my friends Jacopo and Renoy for sharing with me an important and lasting passion, the pleasure of discovery and the magic of wonder. Thanks to the Spartans (Alessandro, Elia, Federico, Giacomo) for sharing thoughts and opinions about the world every day and supporting me. Special thanks to the owner of Play Point, the former game shop on Via Padova in Milan, for introducing me to an incredible world and recommending wonderful games.

strings.A platform game's jump is a designed cur: A platform game's jump is a designed curve, not just an upward movement. Follow coin rows across ground, pits, pipes and raised blocks. Hit question blocks from below: the first releases a moving mushroom that doubles your height and lets you break ordinary bricks; the others release coins. Land on walking obstacles to clear them. Hold or release {cross} to change the jump arc, and hold {square} to run. Hold Down to crouch, or combine Down and {cross} for a crouched jump. Hold Down on the second pipe to enter a separate coin room; its horizontal exit leads back up to the surface. Damage shrinks a grown character; another hit while small, or a fall, returns you to the beginning. Catch the final flag high for a larger score.

strings.Sonic the Hedgehog turns speed into a wa: Sonic the Hedgehog turns speed into a way of reading the landscape. Build momentum on slopes, choose between high and low routes, and use the ring trails to judge your jumps. Curl into a ball while moving to roll through enemies; steer against your movement to brake. A full loop rewards enough speed, while a spring opens the higher route above a curved underpass. At rest, charge a rolling start and release it. A hit scatters your rings: recover them before they disappear, because another hit without rings returns you to the start or the starpost. The starpost banks collected rings. A level finishing straight leads to the spinning sign.
strings.Portal makes momentum part of a spatial: Portal makes momentum part of a spatial puzzle. Connect marked surfaces in four original chambers: cross a wall, turn a fall into distance, carry a cube onto an upper pressure plate, then build speed in a floor-to-ceiling loop and redirect it toward a high exit. Speed survives each crossing while its direction follows the portal. A dotted arc previews the current route. Choose surfaces with {right_stick} or {touchpad}; carry and release the cube nearby. Pressure plates stay active only while supporting the cube.
strings.Explore Green Hill Zone Act 1 with simpl: Explore Green Hill Zone Act 1 with simplified shapes and the original arrangement of slopes, bridges, platforms, rings and enemies. Choose a high or low route, build enough momentum for the loop, and roll through the curved tunnels. Ring trails help you read each jump. Curl into a ball while moving to attack; steer against your movement to brake. At rest, charge a rolling start and release it. A hit scatters your rings: recover them before they disappear. Another hit without rings returns you to the start or the last starpost, with no rings. Cross the spinning sign at the end of the final straight to finish.
